definitions.explanation: The polite form of だから, used to indicate cause and effect in formal speech.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}みです。ですから、{会社|かいしゃ}には{行|い}きません。
examples.english: Tomorrow is a holiday. Therefore, I won't go to the office.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まっています。ですから、{遅|おく}れました。
examples.english: The train has stopped. That's why I was late.

examples.japanese: ですから、{気|き}をつけてください。

notes: ですから is the polite version of だから, appropriate for formal situations and polite speech. It connects a reason to its consequence. In very formal writing, したがって (therefore) may be used instead.
